nodes.name: Eq. (1.1): focusing NLS with inverse-square potential
nodes.statement: i\partial_t u + \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u &= 0, \quad u(0,\cdot)=u_0\in H^1(\rn),
nodes.statement_short: The Cauchy problem $i\partial_t u+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u+|u|^{p-1}u=0$, $u(0)=u_0\in H^1$.
nodes.label: inls

nodes.name: Hardy's inequality
nodes.statement: c_*\intrn \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \le \intrn |\nabla u|^2 dx, \quad u\in H^1(\rn).
nodes.label: hardy

nodes.name: Strong solution and maximal existence time
nodes.statement: We consider strong solutions $u=u(t,x)\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$, where $T>0$ is the maximum time of existence of $u$.

nodes.name: Eq. (1.3): conservation of mass
nodes.statement: \Vert u(t)\Vert_{L^2_x} \equiv \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2_x},
nodes.label: mass

nodes.name: Eq. (1.4): conservation of energy $E(u)$
nodes.statement: E(u(t))=\frac12 \intrn|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\diff x - \frac{c}{2}\int_{\rn}\frac{|u(t,x)|^2}{|x|^2}dx - \frac{1}{p+1}\intrn|u(t,x)|^{p+1}\diff x \equiv E(u_0).
nodes.statement_short: Energy $E(u)=\frac12\int|\nabla u|^2-\frac c2\int|u|^2/|x|^2-\frac1{p+1}\int|u|^{p+1}$ is conserved.
nodes.label: energy

nodes.name: Global solution
nodes.statement: A solution is called global if $T=+\infty$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (local well-posedness; Theorem 5.1 of Okazawa–Suzuki–Yokota)
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$. For any initial value $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$, there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$. Moreover, the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$. Finally, if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
nodes.statement_short: For $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $H^1$ data, (1.1) has a unique maximal solution with blow-up alternative; global if $L^2$-subcritical.
conclusions: there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$.
if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
nodes.label: local.thm

nodes.name: Symmetries of the equation: time translation, phase and scaling invariance
nodes.statement: More precisely, if $u(t,x)$ solves~\eqref{inls}, then so do: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $u_{t_0}(t,x)=u(t-t_0,x)$, for all $t_0\in\R$ (time translation invariance); \item $u_{\gamma_0}(t,x)=e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$, for all $\gamma_0\in\R$ (phase invariance); \item $u_{\lambda_0}(t,x)=\lambda_0^{2/(p-1)}u(\lambda_0^2t,\lambda_0x)$, for all $\lambda_0>0$ (scaling invariance). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Solutions of (1.1) are invariant under time translation, phase rotation and the scaling $\lambda_0^{2/(p-1)}u(\lambda_0^2t,\lambda_0x)$.

nodes.name: Remark: no translation/Galilean invariance; Noether origin of mass and energy
nodes.statement: Note that \eqref{inls} with $c>0$ is not invariant under space translations and Galilean transformations. The symmetries (a) and (b) are obvious and give rise, via Noether's theorem, to the invariance of the energy and the mass, respectively.

nodes.name: Hardy functional $H(u)$
nodes.statement: For our analysis it is convenient to introduce the {\em Hardy functional}, defined on $H^1(\rn)$ by \[ H(u)=\int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx -c\int_{\rn}\frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: $H(u)=\int|\nabla u|^2-c\int|u|^2/|x|^2$ on $H^1(\rn)$.

nodes.name: Energy in terms of the Hardy functional
nodes.statement: Using $H$, the energy can be rewritten as \[ E(u)=\frac12 H(u) - \frac{1}{p+1}\Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}. \]

nodes.name: Eq. (1.5): equivalence of $H(u)$ with $\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2}^2$
nodes.statement: \left(1-\frac{c}{c_*}\right) \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx\le H(u)\le \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx.
nodes.statement_short: For $c\in(0,c_*]$, $(1-c/c_*)\|\nabla u\|^2\le H(u)\le\|\nabla u\|^2$.
nodes.label: hardy2

nodes.name: Blow-up criterion in terms of the Hardy functional
nodes.statement: In particular, for $c\in(0,c_*)$, $H(u)$ defines on $H^1(\rn)$ a seminorm equivalent to $\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2}$. A solution $u(t)$ therefore blows up at time $T>0$ if and only if $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: For $c<c_*$, $H$ is a seminorm equivalent to $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2$, so blow-up at $T$ iff $H(u(t))\to+\infty$.
conclusions: $H(u)$ defines on $H^1(\rn)$ a seminorm equivalent to $\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2}$.
A solution $u(t)$ therefore blows up at time $T>0$ if and only if $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$.

nodes.name: Remark: homogeneity of degree $-2$ of $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $H(u)$ scales as $\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2}^2$ under space dilations. More precisely, the self-adjoint operator $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$ associated with the positive semi-definite quadratic form $H(u)$ is homogeneous of degree $-2$.\footnote{Note that the self-adjoint operator associated with $H(u)$ is unique when $c\le c_*-1$, as $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$ is essentially self-adjoint on $C_0^\infty(\rn\sm\{0\})$ in this case. For $c_*-1<c\le c_*$, this operator has deficiency indices $(1,1)$ and so admits a one-parameter family of self-adjoint extensions in $L^2(\rn)$. See \cite{visan0,kalf} for more details.} The scaling symmetry (c) above is a crucial consequence of this fact.
nodes.statement_short: $H$ scales like $\|\nabla u\|^2$: the operator $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$ is homogeneous of degree $-2$, which yields the scaling symmetry.

nodes.name: $L^2$ scaling and $L^2$ critical equation
nodes.statement: Now, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$ yields $2/(p-1)=N/2$ and, as in the classical case $c=0$, \eqref{inls} is invariant under the {\em $L^2$ scaling} \[ u(t,x) \to u_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2 t, \lambda x) \quad (\lambda>0). \] This transformation preserves the $L^2$ norm and \eqref{inls} is called {\em $L^2$ critical}.
nodes.statement_short: For $p=1+4/N$ the scaling $u_\lambda=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2t,\lambda x)$ preserves the $L^2$ norm; (1.1) is then called $L^2$ critical.

nodes.name: Standing waves correspond to solutions of the stationary equation (1.6)
nodes.statement: $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$ is a (global) solution of~\eqref{inls} if and only if $\ffi\in H^1(\rn)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation \begin{equation} \Delta\ffi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\ffi - \ffi + |\ffi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\ffi=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $e^{it}\varphi$ solves (1.1) iff $\varphi\in H^1$ solves $\Delta\varphi+c|x|^{-2}\varphi-\varphi+|\varphi|^{4/N}\varphi=0$.
conclusions: $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$ is a (global) solution of~\eqref{inls} if and only if $\ffi\in H^1(\rn)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation

nodes.name: Eq. (1.6): stationary equation for standing waves
nodes.statement: \Delta\ffi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\ffi - \ffi + |\ffi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\ffi=0.
nodes.label: sinls

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the ground state for $c=0$
nodes.statement: For $c=0$, it is well known that the ground state is unique, up to the symmetries of \eqref{sinls}. More precisely, there exists a unique positive radial solution $Q\in H^1(\rn)$ of \eqref{sinls}, and $\mathcal{G}=\{e^{i\gamma_0}Q(\cdot - x_0) : \gamma_0\in\real, \ x_0\in\rn\}$.
conclusions: there exists a unique positive radial solution $Q\in H^1(\rn)$ of \eqref{sinls}

nodes.name: Open problem: uniqueness of the ground state for $c>0$
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, for $c>0$, we are not aware of any uniqueness result for \eqref{sinls} on $\rn$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (sharp global existence below the ground-state mass)
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$. If $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}, \end {equation} then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
nodes.statement_short: If $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<M_{\mathrm{gs}}$ then the $L^2$ critical solution is global.
conclusions: then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
nodes.label: global.thm

nodes.name: Eq. (1.7): subcritical mass condition $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_{\mathrm{gs}}$
nodes.statement: \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs},
nodes.label: sharp

nodes.name: Idea of the proof of Theorem 2 via the energy inequality (1.8)
nodes.statement: The proof of this theorem relies on the inequality \begin{equation} E(u)\ge \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\rn), \end{equation} which follows from a sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality established in Section~\ref{global.sec}. Indeed, since the $L^2$ norm and the energy are conserved, \eqref{posE} immediately yields an \emph{a priori} bound on $H(u(t))$ --- and hence on $\Vert\nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}$ --- in the case $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}$. Namely, we have \begin{equation} H(u(t)) \le 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1}, \end{equation} which implies global existence.
nodes.statement_short: Conservation plus $E(u)\ge\frac12H(u)(1-(\|u\|/M_{\mathrm{gs}})^{4/N})$ gives an a priori bound on $H(u(t))$, hence global existence.

nodes.name: Eq. (1.8): energy lower bound $E(u)\ge\frac12 H(u)(1-(\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}/M_{\mathrm{gs}})^{4/N})$
nodes.statement: E(u)\ge \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\rn),
nodes.statement_short: Energy is bounded below by a positive multiple of $H(u)$ when the mass is below $M_{\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.label: posE

nodes.name: Eq. (1.9): a priori bound on $H(u(t))$ below the minimal mass
nodes.statement: H(u(t)) \le 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1},
nodes.label: subcritical

nodes.name: Eq. (1.10): the minimal mass blow-up family $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$
nodes.statement: S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right).
nodes.statement_short: Explicit pseudo-conformal blow-up profile built from a ground state $Q$.
nodes.label: S1.def

nodes.name: Remark: self-similar profile of $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$
nodes.statement: Note that these solutions present a self-similar profile, in the sense that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, there exists $\lam(t)>0$ such that $|S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x)|=\lam(t)^{N/2}Q(\lam(t)x)$. Hence, up to a time-dependent $L^2$ rescaling, $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ keeps the same shape as $Q$ while blowing up.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (classification of minimal mass blow-up solutions)
nodes.statement: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$. Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
nodes.statement_short: Every minimal mass finite-time blow-up solution is $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ for some ground state $Q$, $\lambda_0>0$, $\gamma_0$.
assumptions: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$.
conclusions: Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
nodes.label: main.thm

nodes.name: Natural energy space $\mathcal{H}$ at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: The natural energy space associated with \eqref{inls}, $\mathcal{H}=\{u\in L^2(\rn) : H(u)<+\infty\}$, then satisfies $H^1(\rn)\subsetneq\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Remark: how Theorem 1 is proved and why it fails at $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: For $c\in(0,c_*)$, Theorem~\ref{local.thm} above was proved in \cite{suzuki}, by adapting to $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$ Cazenave's proof of \cite[Theorems~3.3.9]{cazenave}, originally developed to deal with $-\Delta$ in bounded domains, where dispersive estimates are not available. This approach allows one to obtain existence of local (in time) solutions \cite[Theorems~3.3.5]{cazenave}, but an additional uniqueness result is required to obtain the full well-posedness result \cite[Theorems~3.3.9]{cazenave}. In \cite{suzuki}, uniqueness relies on the Strichartz estimates for $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$, which were established in \cite{burq}. Unfortunately, as pointed out on p.~521 of \cite{burq}, these estimates break down at the threshold value $c=c_*$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1 follows Cazenave's energy method with uniqueness from Strichartz estimates, which break down at $c=c_*$.

nodes.name: Open problem: uniqueness (well-posedness) at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: Hence, the existence of local in time solutions is ensured by \cite{suzuki}, but it is not clear if and how uniqueness can be proved.

nodes.name: Open problem: compactness (Proposition 4) at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: Note that, for $c=c_*$, inequality \eqref{crucial} also breaks down, and we do not know how to prove the crucial Proposition~\ref{compact.prop}.

nodes.name: Weinstein functional $J^{p,N}$
nodes.statement: Consider the Weinstein functional \[ J^{p,N}(u):=\frac{H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|u\|^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}_{L^2}}{\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Proposition 1 (existence of minimizers of the Weinstein functional)
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$, \[ \alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u) \] is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation \begin{equation} N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0. \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \alpha_{p,N}=2\frac{\|Q\|_{L^2}^{p-1}}{p+1}. \end{equation} In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: $\inf J^{p,N}$ is attained at a positive radial $Q$ solving the Euler–Lagrange equation, with $\alpha_{p,N}=2\|Q\|_{L^2}^{p-1}/(p+1)$; critical minimizers rescale to solutions of (1.6).
conclusions: is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation
In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.label: minimization.prop

nodes.name: Minimization of the Weinstein functional
nodes.statement: \alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u)
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Eq. (2.1): Euler–Lagrange equation for minimizers
nodes.statement: N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: EL

nodes.name: Eq. (2.2): value of $\alpha_{p,N}$
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: sharpestimate

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*} Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing. Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$. Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$. Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}. Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Direct method: scaling-invariance of $J$, symmetrize and normalize a minimizing sequence, pass to the weak limit by compact radial embedding, then read off the Euler–Lagrange equation and rescale.

nodes.name: Remark 1 (phase invariance, equal mass of minimizers, positivity/radiality)
nodes.statement:
oindent (a) Note that, by phase invariance of $J^{p,N}$, if $u$ is a minimizer so is $e^{i	heta}u, \ 	heta\in\R$. \medskip 
oindent (b) For $p=1+ rac{4}{N}$, the Pohozaev identity for \eqref{sinls} implies that any minimizer $u$ of $J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}$ satisfies $E(u)=0$, that is \[ H(u)= rac{1}{1+ rac{2}{N}}\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}, \] and so  egin{equation} J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}(u) = rac{H(u)\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}} = rac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{1+ rac{2}{N}}. \end{equation} Therefore, all minimizers have the same mass. \medskip 
oindent (c) The proof of Proposition~ef{charact.prop} below shows that all minimizers are positive and radial, up to a global phase factor.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers are phase-invariant; by Pohozaev every critical minimizer has $E(u)=0$ and all minimizers share the same mass; they are positive and radial up to phase.
nodes.label: gs_scaling.rem

nodes.name: Eq. (2.5): value of $J$ at a critical minimizer
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: valueofmin

nodes.name: Definition 1 (ground states, $\mathcal{G}$, minimal mass $M_{\mathrm{gs}}$)
nodes.statement: In the case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, we call {\em ground states} the minimizers of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$ that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}. We denote the set of ground states by $\mathcal{G}$. In view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem}~(b), there exists $M_\mathrm{gs}>0$ such that $\Vert Q\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ for all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$. We call $M_\mathrm{gs}$ the {\em minimal mass}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Ground states are positive radial minimizers of $J$ solving (1.6); they all have mass $M_{\mathrm{gs}}$, the minimal mass.
nodes.label: gs.def

nodes.name: Remark 2 ($L^2$ scaling of ground states)
nodes.statement: The $L^2$ scaling $u_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda{x})$ yields \[ H(u_\lambda)=\lambda^2H(u), \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}, \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}=\lambda^2 \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}, \quad \text{hence} \quad J^{p,N}(u_\lambda)=J^{p,N}(u). \] Therefore, if $Q$ is a ground state, then $Q_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x)$ is again a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, satisfying $\Vert Q_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and the rescaled Euler--Lagrange equation \[ \Delta Q_\lambda+ \frac{c}{|x|^2}Q_\lambda-\lambda^{2} Q_\lambda + |Q_\lambda|^{\frac{4}{N}}Q_\lambda=0. \] It follows from Remark~\ref{minmass.rem} below that the ground states are the solutions of \eqref{sinls} with smallest mass.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: $Q_\lambda=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda\cdot)$ is again a minimizer with mass $M_{\mathrm{gs}}$ solving a rescaled equation; ground states are the smallest-mass solutions of (1.6).
nodes.label: scaling.rem

nodes.name: Corollary 1 (sharp Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality)
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$ and $u\in H^1(\rn)$, we have \begin{equation} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}, \end{equation} where \[ \alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}} \quad\text{in the critical case} \quad p=1+\frac{4}{N}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: $\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}\le\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|u\|_{L^2}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}$ with sharp constant from the ground state mass.
nodes.label: GN.cor

nodes.name: Eq. (2.6): sharp Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)},
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: GN

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded. We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \] Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \] Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Bound $H(u(t))$ via the energy, the sharp Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality and conservation laws, then use the blow-up alternative.

nodes.name: Standing assumption: $L^2$ critical nonlinearity $p=1+4/N$
nodes.statement: From now on and for the rest of the paper, unless specified otherwise, we focus on the $L^2$ critical nonlinearity $p=1+\frac4N$.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (pseudo-conformal invariance)
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}. Then, for all $T\in\R$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: The pseudo-conformal transform $u_T$ of a global solution is again a solution on $(-\infty,T)$ with the same mass.
assumptions: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}.
conclusions: the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.label: pseudo-conf.lem

nodes.name: Pseudo-conformal transformation
nodes.statement: for all $T\in\R$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \]
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives. For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \] It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of $\partial_t u_T$, $\Delta u_T$, the nonlinear and potential terms, and substitution into (1.1).

nodes.name: Remark 3 (every solution of (1.6) has mass at least $M_{\mathrm{gs}}$)
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} that any solution $\ffi$ of \eqref{sinls} satisfies $\|\ffi\|_{L^2}\ge M_\mathrm{gs}$. Otherwise, applying Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} with $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$, one could construct a finite time blow-up solution below the minimal mass threshold, which would contradict our global well-posedness result, Theorem~\ref{global.thm}.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise the pseudo-conformal transform of $e^{it}\varphi$ would blow up below the minimal mass, contradicting Theorem 2.
nodes.label: minmass.rem

nodes.name: Proposition 2 (explicit minimal mass blow-up solutions)
nodes.statement: For all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $T\in\R$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$, the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right), \end{equation} is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ is a minimal mass solution on $(-\infty,T)$ blowing up at rate $C/(T-t)$.
conclusions: is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$.
nodes.label: blow-up_sol.prop

nodes.name: Eq. (3.1): definition of $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$
nodes.statement: S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right),
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.label: S2.def

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement: The proposition is a simple consequence of Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} applied to the global solution \[ u_{Q,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\lambda_0^2 t}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x), \] which is given by applying the scaling and phase symmetries to the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{it}Q(x)$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 1 to the standing wave rescaled and phase-shifted by the symmetries.

nodes.name: Remark 4 (all $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are symmetry images of one solution $S$)
nodes.statement: Note that the blow-up solutions of the family exhibited in Proposition~\ref{blow-up_sol.prop} can all be retrieved from the solution \[ S(t,x) := S_{0,1,0}(t,x) = e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4t}} e^{-\frac{i}{t}} \frac{1}{|t|^{N/2}}Q\left(-\frac{x}{t}\right), \] defined on $(-\infty,0)$ and which blows up at $t=0$ with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{|t|}\quad \text{as } t\uparrow0, \] for some $C>0$. Indeed, all the solutions $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are equal to $S$, up to the symmetries (a), (b) and (c) stated in the introduction. Namely, if we apply the changes $u(t,x)\to \lambda_0^{-N/2}u(\lambda_0^{-2}t,\lambda_0^{-1}x)$, $u(t,x)\to u(t-T,x)$ and finally $u(t,x)\to e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$ to $S$, we obtain $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Every member of the family is obtained from $S(t,x)=S_{0,1,0}$ by the scaling, time-translation and phase symmetries.

nodes.name: Proposition 3 (variational characterization of ground states)
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H^1(\rn)$ be such that \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0. \end{equation} Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Any $v$ with $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_{\mathrm{gs}}$ and $E(v)=0$ is a phase-rotated rescaled ground state.
conclusions: Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.label: charact.prop

nodes.name: Eq. (4.1): $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_{\mathrm{gs}}$ and $E(v)=0$
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement:
It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+ rac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)\le J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer. Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization. Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \intrn  rac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \intrn  rac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert

Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad 	ext{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big( rac{2}{N}\Big)^{ rac{1}{2}} rac{H(|v|)^ rac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \] The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $n$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\inn$. nodes.name: Lemma 2 (concentration-compactness)
nodes.statement:
Let $\{v_n\}_{n\in \N}\subset H^1(n)$ satisfy \[ \lim_{n ightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M<+\infty \quad 	ext{and} \quad \sup_{n\in\N} H(v_n) <+\infty. \] Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \N}$ that satisfies one of the following properties. \medskip 
oindent (V) $\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^q}ightarrow 0$ as $kightarrow\infty$ for all $q\in(2,2^*)$. \medskip 
oindent (D) There are sequences ${w_k},{z_k}\in H^1(n)$ and a constant $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that:  egin{enumerate} \item $\dist(\supp(w_k),\supp(z_k))ightarrow\infty$; \item $|v_k|+|z_k|\le |v_{n_k}|$; \item $\sup_{k\in\N} (\|w_k\|_{H^1}+\|z_k\|_{H^1})<+\infty$; \item $\|w_k\|_{L^2}ightarrow\alpha M$ and $\|z_k\|_{L^2}	o (1-\alpha)M$ as $kightarrow\infty$; \item $\lim_{kightarrow\infty} ig| \int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^q-\int_{n}|w_k|^q-\int_{n}|z_k|^q ig|=0$ for all $q\in[2,2^*)$; \item $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty} ig\{ H(v_{n_k})-H(w_k)-H(z_k)  ig\}\ge 0$. \end{enumerate} \medskip 
oindent (C) There exists $v\in H^1(n)$ and a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset n$ such that \[ v_{n_k}(\cdot -y_k)ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(n), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*). \]

conclusions: Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \N}$ that satisfies one of the following properties.
(D) There are sequences ${w_k},{z_k}\in H^1(\rn)$ and a constant $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that:
(C) There exists $v\in H^1(\rn)$ and a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset \rn$ such that \[ v_{n_k}(\cdot -y_k)\rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\rn), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*). \]

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4
nodes.statement:
The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $n$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~ef{charact.prop}. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(n)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\Big\{ rac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})- rac{1}{p+1}\int_{n} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}= rac{1}{2}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[  egin{split} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\le rac{1}{2}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) - rac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|dx \ &\le\limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\le 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (ef{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\ge 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad 	ext{and} \quad E(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad	ext{and}\quad H(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{n}|z_k|^{p+1}dxight)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$. Consequently, by Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(n)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset n$ such that  egin{equation} \wt{v}_{n_k} ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(n), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \wt{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\wt{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(n)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\wt{v}_{n_k}\wto v$ weakly in $H^1(n)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2: Localization.} We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $n$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|ightarrow\infty$ as $kightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}. We start by showing that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\ge R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(n)$, there exists $C\ge0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\le R^{-2}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\le CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$. Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta. \end{equation*} Note that this inequality will still hold if we increase the value of $R$ or pass to a further subsequence. oindent {\em Step~3: Conclusion.} Suppose, without loss of generality, that $y_k	o y^*\inn$. Then \[ v_{n_k}	o v^*=v(\cdot+y^*) \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(n), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*), \] and $v_{n_k}\wto v^*$ weakly in $H^1(n)$. Furthermore, \[  egin{split} H(v_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)=1. \end{split} \] On the other hand, by conservation of the energy, \[  egin{split} E(v_n)&= rac12\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)- rac{1}{p+1}\lambda_n^{-2}\int_{n} |u_n(y)|^{p+1}dy\ &=\lambda_n^{-2} E(u_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}E(u_0)	o 0 \quad 	ext{as} \ n	o\infty. \end{split} \] Hence, by Proposition ef{compact.prop}, there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $\gamma_0\ineal$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that, up to a subsequence,  egin{equation} \lim_{nightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0, \end{equation} where $Q_{\lambda_0}(x)=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2.} We now prove that $u_n$ concentrates all of its mass at $x=0$ as $nightarrow\infty$. We show that, in the sense of distributions, \[ |u_n|^2ightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\delta_0. \] Indeed, for any $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(n)$, using the change of variables $y=\lambda_n^{-1}x$ we find that \[  egin{split} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy &=\int_{n}|u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x)|^2\varphi(\lambda^{-1}_nx)\lambda_n^{-N}dx =\int_{n}|v_n(x)|^2\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx\ &=\int_{n}(|v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2)\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx+\int_{n} |Q(x)|^2\varphi(0)dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2(\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0))dx. \end{split} \] Thus, we obtain \[  egin{split} \Big|\int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy -M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0)\Big| &\le \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty}\int_{n}||v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2|dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2|\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0)|dx. \end{split} \] We conclude this step by noticing that $|v_n|^2$ converges strongly to $|Q|^2$ in $L^1(n)$ from (ef{b}), so the first integral vanishes as $nightarrow\infty$. Since $\lambda_nightarrow\infty$ the second integral also converges to zero by the dominated convergence theorem. Hence, we obtain  egin{equation} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dyightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0). \end{equation} \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~3.} We now show that $u(t)\in\Sigma$ for all $t\in[0,T)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty_0(n)$ be a radial and non-negative function such that $\phi(x)=|x|^2$ for $|x|\le 1$. It is easy to see that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \[ |

By Taylor's formula, for all $r\ineal$ and $h\ineal$ there exists $y\in[r,r+h]$, such that \[ 0\le f(r+h)=f(r)+f'(r)h+ rac{f''(y)}{2}h^2\le f(r)+f'(r)h+C'h^2, \] where $C'=1+\max_{r\ineal} rac{|f'(r)|}{2}>0$. Since the right-hand side is a positive quadratic polynomial, we must have that $|f'(r)|^2-4C'f(r)\le 0$, thus $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$, where $C=4C'>0$. For all $R>0$, we define $\phi_R(x)=R^2\phi(x/R)$, and for all $t\in[0,T)$, \[ \Gamma_R(t)=\int_{n}\phi_R(x)|u(t,x)|^2dx. \] A direct calculation, similar to the proof of Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, yields that \[ \Gamma_R'(t)=2	ext{Re}\int\phi_R ar{u}\partial_tu =-2	ext{Im}\int\phi_R ar{u}(\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u) =2\int
abla\phi_R\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u}

abla\phi_R|^2\le C\phi_R$, to get \[ |\Gamma'_R(t)|\le 2\sqrt{2E(u)}\Big(\int|
abla\phi_R|^2|u|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le C\sqrt{E(u_0)}\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}. \] By integrating between a fixed $t\in[0,T)$ and $t_n$, we obtain, \[ |\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}-\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t_n)}|\le C|t-t_n|. \] Applying (ef{c}) in Step 2, we get \[ \Gamma_R(t_n)=\int_{n} |u_n(x)|^2\phi_R(x)dxightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\phi_R(0)=0. \] Thus, letting $n	o\infty$ in the last inequality, we obtain, for all $t\in [0,T)$ and all $R>0$, \[ \Gamma_R(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] Since the right-hand side of the last expression is independent of $R$, letting $R	o\infty$ yields, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)\in\Sigma \quad	ext{and}\quad 0\le \Gamma(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] From this estimate, we can extend by continuity $\Gamma(t)$ at $t=T$ by setting $\Gamma(T)=0$, from which we also obtain $\Gamma'(T)=0$. Moreover, since $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and $u$ is a solution of~\eqref{inls}, we may apply Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, and by (ef{virialthree}) we obtain $\Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0)$, which finally gives, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ \Gamma(t) = 8E(u_0)(T-t)^2. \] Letting $t=0$, we find, using identity (ef{virialone}) \[ \Gamma(0)=\int |x|^2|u_0|^2= 8E(u_0)T^2 \quad 	ext{and}\quad \Gamma'(0)= 4\int x\cdot\im(\overline{u_0}

ot\in C_0^{\infty}(n)$. Since $\|u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}})=0$, we can deduce from Proposition ef{charact.prop} that there exist $\lambda_1>0$, $\gamma_1\ineal$, and $\wt{Q}\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ u_0(x)=e^{i\gamma_1}e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\lambda_1^{N/2}\wt{Q}(\lambda_1x). \] Finally, we use the pseudo-conformal transformation. We define $	ilde\lambda_0=\lambda_1T>0$ and $	ilde\gamma_0=\gamma_1-\lambda_1^2T\ineal$, and write $u_0$ as \[ u_0(x)=e^{i	ilde\gamma_0}e^{i rac{	ilde\lambda^2_0}{T}} e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0}{T}\Big)^{N/2}\wt{Q}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0x}{T}\Big). \] Thus, $u_0=S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}(0)$, where $S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}$ is defined by (ef{S2.def}). nodes.name: Eq. (4.23): $H^1$ convergence of the rescaled profiles $v_n$
nodes.statement: \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0,
nodes.label: b

nodes.name: Eq. (4.24): mass concentration at the origin
nodes.statement: \int_{\rn}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy\rightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0).

nodes.name: Scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Check that $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under $u\mapsto\mu u(\lambda\cdot)$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Minimizing sequence, reduced to positive radial decreasing functions
nodes.statement: Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Take a minimizing sequence; by $J(|u|)\le J(u)$ and Schwarz symmetrization assume $u_n$ positive, radial, decreasing.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Normalize to $\|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=H(\psi_n)=1$
nodes.statement: Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale to a minimizing sequence $\psi_n$ with unit mass and unit $H$, hence bounded in $H^1$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Extract a weak limit $\psi^*$
nodes.statement: Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak $H^1$ limit and strong $L^{p+1}$ convergence by the compact radial embedding.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: $\psi^*$ is a minimizer with $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$
nodes.statement: By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity gives $J(\psi^*)=\alpha_{p,N}$ and the normalizations are attained.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Euler–Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$
nodes.statement: Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write out the Euler–Lagrange equation (2.3) satisfied by $\psi^*$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Rescale $\psi^*$ to $Q$
nodes.statement: Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the normalizations and set $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ to get (2.1) and (2.2).
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Critical case: rescale minimizers to solutions of (1.6)
nodes.statement: Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: For $p=1+4/N$ the Euler–Lagrange equation becomes (2.4) and an $L^2$ rescaling gives a solution of (1.6).
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Reduce to bounding $H(u(t))$
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded.
nodes.statement_short: By the blow-up alternative it suffices to bound $H(u(t))$ when $\|u_0\|<M_{\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Express $H$ through the energy
nodes.statement: We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Apply the sharp Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $L^{2+4/N}$ norm by $(1+2/N)(\|u\|/M_{\mathrm{gs}})^{4/N}H(u)$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Use conservation laws
nodes.statement: Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Conclude the a priori bound
nodes.statement: It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: $(1-(\|u_0\|/M_{\mathrm{gs}})^{4/N})H(u(t))\le 2E(u_0)$, so $H$ stays bounded.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Compute $\partial_t u_T$ and $\Delta u_T$
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for the time derivative and Laplacian of $u_T$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Compute the nonlinear and potential terms
nodes.statement: For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Both terms pick up the same prefactor $e^{-i|x|^2/4(T-t)}(T-t)^{-N/2-2}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Substitute into the equation
nodes.statement: It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The combination equals the prefactor times the equation for $u$, hence vanishes.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: $v$ and $|v|$ minimize $J$
nodes.statement: It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)\le J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer.
nodes.statement_short: From (2.5) and (4.1), $v$ is a minimizer; so is $|v|$.

nodes.name: Suppose a positive minimizer is not radial
nodes.statement: Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization.
nodes.statement_short: Set up a contradiction with the Schwarz symmetrization $v_0^*$.

nodes.name: Symmetrization strictly decreases $J$
nodes.statement: Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \intrn \frac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \intrn \frac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert \nabla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla v_0\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert v_0\Vert_{L^2}, \] we get $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0^*)<J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0)$, a contradiction. We deduce that $|v|$ is radial.
nodes.statement_short: Strict rearrangement inequality for $\int|v|^2/|x|^2$ gives $J(v_0^*)<J(v_0)$, a contradiction; $|v|$ is radial.

nodes.name: $|v|$ is a rescaled ground state
nodes.statement: Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad \text{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big(\frac{2}{N}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{H(|v|)^\frac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: From the Euler–Lagrange equation (2.4), $|v|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0\cdot)$ for some $Q\in\mathcal G$.

nodes.name: Reduce to constancy of the phase $w=v/|v|$
nodes.statement: The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $\rn$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\in\rn$.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to show $w$ is constant.

nodes.name: Split $\|\nabla v\|^2$ into modulus and phase parts
nodes.statement:
Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $e(\overline{w}
abla w)\equiv 0$, thus \[ |
abla v|^2=|
abla(|v|)|^2+|v|^2|
abla w|^2+2|v|
abla(|v|)\cdot e(\overline{w}
abla w) \] and \[ \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2=\|
abla (|v|)\|_{L^2}^2+\int_{n} |v|^2|
abla w|^2dx. \]
nodes.statement_short:
$\|
abla v\|^2=\|
abla|v|\|^2+\int|v|^2|
abla w|^2$.

nodes.name: Conclude $w$ constant
nodes.statement: Together with Hardy's inequality, this implies that, if $|\nabla w|\neq 0$ then $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction. Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: If $\nabla w\ne0$ then $J(|v|)<J(v)$, a contradiction; so $w$ is constant.

nodes.name: Overview of the argument
nodes.statement: The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $\rn$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~\ref{charact.prop}.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: rule out (V) and (D), prove localization of the translations, then apply Proposition 3.

nodes.name: Step 1: compactness in $L^q$
nodes.statement: {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(\rn)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Big\{\frac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\rn} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}=\frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds.
